Okanagan (Syilx)

This Syilx Okanagan path follows Nation-published accounts of colonial disruption, continuing cross-border ties, institutional advocacy and salmon restoration. It distinguishes the broader people, the Alliance and individual communities rather than using these names interchangeably.

01

Identity and context

Syilx is a people’s name used alongside Okanagan in sources about communities across modern borders.

Read the sources [1] Syilx Okanagan Nation / Okanagan Nation Alliance

02

A path for deeper reading

Focus the next stage of research on: Syilx-authored history, nsyilxcən language, territory and distinct political communities. The sources below are selected reading paths; their authorship, dates and community scope should guide how they are used.

Read the sources [1] Syilx Okanagan Nation / Okanagan Nation Alliance [2] Syilx Okanagan Nation / Okanagan Nation Alliance [3] Syilx Okanagan Nation educational resource

03

Borders did not end community continuity

The Nation’s history explains how colonial borders and displacement separated families while kinship continued across what are now Canada and the United States. It explicitly describes Sinixt continuity. A past administrative declaration should not be treated as evidence that a people disappeared.

Read the sources [2] Syilx Okanagan Nation / Okanagan Nation Alliance

04

An organization and a history of advocacy

The history page traces the Alliance’s development, while the partnership account recounts engagement with BC Hydro leading to a 2011 arrangement. These are institutional narratives. Original agreements and the different member communities’ accounts remain important further readings.

Read the sources [2] Syilx Okanagan Nation / Okanagan Nation Alliance [1] Syilx Okanagan Nation / Okanagan Nation Alliance

05

A lake connected with restoration work

The fish-passage account describes efforts to reconnect Okanagan Lake with salmon habitat and explains monitoring goals. The dated Kelowna lake photograph introduces that waterbody; it does not show the fishway or demonstrate restoration success. The educational timeline offers a separate route into community commemoration.

Read the sources [4] Syilx Okanagan Nation / Okanagan Nation Alliance [3] Syilx Okanagan Nation educational resource

History of the Partnership — the Nation’s account of BC Hydro engagement ↗

The Nation recounts advocacy and negotiations leading to its 2011 relationship arrangement with BC Hydro. This institutional account is distinct from the underlying permits and agreement.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Actual complete main historical body, reader lines5–14; duplicated 2011 paragraph is one passage, not another work.

Review recorded: October 28, 2026

Access note: Normal HTTP200 HTML read. Court decisions, permits, agreement terms and current benefits/outcomes uninspected. Numerical infrastructure claims and present legal conclusions not adopted.

https://syilx.org/governance/partnerships/bc-hydro-enduring-relationship/history-of-the-partnership/

Indigenous-ledSyilx Okanagan Nation / Okanagan Nation AllianceSource 2

History — selected Syilx Okanagan community and organizational account ↗

The Nation links colonial borders and displacement with continuing kinship and explains the Okanagan Nation Alliance’s institutional development.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Actual history, border/continuity and Tribal Council body, reader lines5–27. Sinixt continuity is the source’s attributed statement; it is not reduced to a past administrative label.

Review recorded: October 28, 2026

Access note: Normal HTTP200 HTML read. Original border, band, constitutional and title records uninspected. This is a Nation-published interpretation, not a current legal determination or one government for all communities.

https://syilx.org/about/history/

Syilx Historic Timeline — selected education and commemoration entries ↗

A three-page educational chronology connects residential-school history with later community projects and commemoration. It is one compilation rather than many primary-source inspections.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Actual three-page extracted timeline body read; synthesis limited to 1990–2024 organization, community films, committees and commemorative-work entries. No images reused.

Review recorded: October 28, 2026

Access note: Normal HTTP200 PDF/text read. Original policies, school records, films and underlying investigations uninspected. Broad legal explanations, totals, and the 2021 remains claim are not adopted as independently verified findings.

https://learn.syilx.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/6/2024/10/SIRS-Timeline.pdf

kłusxnitkʷ Okanagan Lake Dam Fish Passage — selected project explanation ↗

The Nation explains fish-passage restoration and monitoring as part of its relationship with Okanagan Lake. Goals and reported progress are distinguished from independent ecological evaluation.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Actual background, project-goal and restoration paragraphs, reader lines5–31, and monitoring explanation54–56. Later FAQ read but numerical/current assertions not used.

Review recorded: October 28, 2026

Access note: Normal public body read. Design renderings, monitoring feed, photos, permits and underlying studies uninspected. No current counts, flood-safety assurance or complete-recovery claim adopted; lake photograph does not show the fishway.

https://syilx.org/programs-services-and-initiatives/fisheries-and-natural-resources/ntytyix-chief-salmon/klusxnitk%CA%B7-okanagan-lake-dam-fish-passage/
